evaluations.ideal_answer: To design a subnetting scheme for a large enterprise network, I would use Variable Length Subnet Masks (VLSM) and Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) notation to maximize the number of hosts and simplify management. For 500 subnets, I would start with a /16 subnet, allowing for 65536 possible subnets, and then use VLSM to allocate /24 subnets for smaller networks and /30 for point-to-point links. This approach enables easy management, scalability, and efficient IP address allocation.

evaluations.ideal_answer: To verify that a misconfigured router does not propagate issues to the entire network, I would first use BGP route reflection and route filtering to contain the impact. Then, I would analyze network segmentation and implement measures to prevent suboptimal routing decisions, such as configuring route dampening and using prefix lists to filter out problematic routes. For example, in a network using BGP, configuring a route reflector with appropriate filtering can help prevent a misconfigured edge router from advertising incorrect routes to the rest of the network.
